root_idea.summary: The root primarily concerns the leg or foot, and extends to walking on foot, pedestrians, and several figurative or transferred uses based on support, standing, extremity, or movement.
root_idea.development: The lexical development proceeds from the bodily leg or foot to going on foot and the people or animals characterized by it; other branches include objects' lower extremities, groups likened to a leg or swarm, and a number of specialized idioms. The meanings man and male human are treated as a distinct lexical branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized pedestrian citation form.
Displayed under the singular masculine-human citation form.
رِجَال is the plural associated with رَجُل and is represented under the singular dictionary headword; its Quranic on-foot construction remains separately defined.
Displayed under the normalized anatomical citation form رِجْل.

senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quranic expression contrasting foot soldiers with mounted forces.

senses.definition: A man; a male human being.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural رِجَال is also used in the Quran; in one Quranic passage it can include male jinn as well as human men. The word denotes the male person rather than a generic human being.

senses.definition: A man presented with the qualities of manhood, firmness, or fortitude.
senses.usage_conditions: In particular descriptions, the word can foreground manliness and resolve in addition to identifying a male person; this is an evaluative contextual emphasis, not a restriction to a special social class.

senses.definition: People proceeding on foot; on foot rather than mounted.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural رجال in the construction فَرِجَالًا أَوْ رُكْبَانًا contrasts walking or infantry movement with riding.

senses.definition: The leg or foot of a human being or animal.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the plural أَرْجُل for feet or legs and also the singular رِجْل in a bodily-foot construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go on foot, remain or travel without a riding animal, or be strong and enduring in walking; of an animal, to endure long travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the corresponding verbal noun and descriptions of a person or beast able to walk or travel on foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be large in the leg or foot.
To suffer a complaint or unwanted condition affecting the leg or foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used with مِنْ رِجْلِهِ for being affected in the leg or foot by something disliked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast, to have whiteness in one hind leg or foot while the rest of the limbs lack that marking; أَرْجَل is the corresponding epithet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form رَجْلَاء is used for a female animal with the described marking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hair of a texture between lankness and crisp curliness: wavy or moderately curled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective can also describe a person having this kind of hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To comb, arrange, wash, or anoint hair; to make hair hang down or become moderately arranged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive form may concern one's own hair or another person's hair; the associated noun denotes combed hair or hair-grooming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hit or hurt someone in the leg or foot.
To suspend or confine a sheep or goat by its hind leg or by pressing it with the feet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The detailed descriptions vary between hanging the animal by its leg and restraining its folded limbs with the feet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, to give birth with the legs appearing before the head.
To leave a young animal with its mother so that it may suck whenever it wishes; of the young animal, to suck its mother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to young camels and also to lambs, kids, calves, or colts; it can describe a mother whose udder is left unbound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a stallion, to mate with mares or to be sent among them.
To press or compress a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized euphemistic bodily or sexual expression in the cited lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man much given to sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional usage attributed to Arabs of Yemen; it is a characterization of sexual activity, not the ordinary meaning of رَجُل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who is or makes herself like a man in some qualities, states, appearance, or speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a marked classical description of a woman as manlike, distinct from the ordinary male-human noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perfect, complete, strong, or manly in bodily vigor or comparable qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally or in comparison between two men; this classical evaluative use is broader than simple reference to a male person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The making or rendering of something strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun use of Form II.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone go on foot or alight from a riding animal.
To grant delay or respite; to leave someone alone for a while.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form IV meaning unrelated to making someone walk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To descend into a well by one's own legs, without being lowered or suspended by a rope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be construed with the well directly or with فِي.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce fire while using the hands and feet to hold the two pieces of wood because one is alone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle denotes the person who performs this operation with the lower piece held by the foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a man or rise to manhood; of a woman, to become manlike in some qualities or circumstances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a derived-verb use, distinct from the noun for a male human.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the day, to become advanced, with the sun somewhat high, or to pass below the walls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression likening the day or sun to a person standing or alighting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to alternate or mix the paces called العَنَق and الهَمْلَجَة.
To take or seize a man by his leg or foot.
To speak, recite, compose, or perform something extemporaneously, without prior preparation or deliberation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a speech, poem, name, or other production delivered without premeditation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act independently in an opinion, without consulting others, and persist in the position adopted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used imperatively for keeping to one's undertaken affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect or come upon a detached group of locusts for roasting or cooking.
To set up or use a cooking pot for preparing food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized derived-verb use associated with مِرْجَل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To desire or request to go on foot.
A figurative state of setting about an affair that presses heavily or urgently upon a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Derived from the image of standing on one leg; it is an idiom rather than an anatomical meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be in fear that something may escape or be missed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use in the expression أَنَا عَلَى رِجْلٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular one-legged idol of the Hijaz.
The bright star Rigel, regarded as the foot of Orion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized astronomical name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Names of certain plants, including plants associated with the appellations رِجْل الغراب and رِجْل الجراد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The botanical referents vary by cited usage; the expression is not the ordinary anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A method of binding a camel's udder so that its young cannot suck and the binding will not come undone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression also supplies a metaphor for something made firm or difficult to undo.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an affair or a person's livelihood to become difficult, constrained, or hard to manage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom based on the secure udder-binding described in the associated lexical entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular branding instrument or brand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object-name.

other_classical_meanings.headword_arabic: رِجْل الباب / رِجْل القوس / رِجْل السهم
other_classical_meanings.definition: The foot, heel, lower curved end, or extremity of an object such as a door, bow, or arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The precise part varies with the object; the common extension is a supporting or lower extremity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A canal, channel, or watercourse through which water runs from stony ground to softer or level ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related noun may also denote a place where water collects or a water-fed tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A part, portion, or lateral half of a thing, including part of a carcass or a half of a water carrier.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is figurative or synecdochic in the cited expressions and does not mean an anatomical leg there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leg or pair of legs of trousers or drawers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular expression can refer collectively to the two-legged garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swarm, detached group, or numerous assemblage of locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective noun may be masculine or feminine and need not have a regular singular.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An army or numerous armed group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred collective use likening an army to a swarm or gathered group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A share or portion in someone's property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression لِي فِي مَالِكَ رِجْلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A time or period during a particular person's lifetime.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiom parallel to saying that something occurred during a person's time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Precedence or priority in a contest or ordering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when handlers of camels contend over who has precedence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distress, straitened livelihood, pressing want, misfortune, calamity, or poverty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative classical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who sleeps much.
A foul-mouthed, ill-disposed, or socially withdrawn man who does not mix easily with others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized characterization associated with the epithet قاذورة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blank paper without writing.
A herd or detached group of wild animals gathered together.
Rugged, hard, or stony ground or a road difficult to traverse, where movement is possible only on foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited descriptions include both rough mountain roads and level ground made difficult by abundant stones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Manhood, manliness, or the condition of being a male human; also strength or vehemence in walking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun has both a manhood branch and a walking-strength branch in the cited lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The successive bringing forth of young animals one after another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported specifically of sheep or goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person known for running or traveling on foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited plural refers to named men famed for running on foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pedestrian or footman, especially one without a riding animal; of a beast, one capable of enduring long travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader individual and animal application is distinct from the Quranic collective sense infantry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ram used by a shepherd to carry or convey his utensils.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hunters, fowlers, or fishermen accustomed to capturing animals, birds, or fish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smallage or a related garden herb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal plant name of the Sawad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who gives birth to male children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also explained as the equivalent of مُذْكِر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A copper or stone-and-copper cooking pot, or any vessel in which food is cooked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also denote a large cooking pot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A comb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal homonym or specialized branch of the same written form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A figured or variegated Yemeni garment or cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usage includes a type of burd garment and cloth associated with full-grown men.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker of cooking pots.
A skin removed beginning from one hind leg or from the part where the leg is attached.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The corresponding animal may be a sheep, goat, or ram.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin or leather vessel filled with wine.
A garment bearing figures of men or other figured decoration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes both human figures and ornamentation in the borders.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Locusts whose wing traces are visible on the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gazelle whose hind leg has been caught in a snare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A foreleg caught in the snare receives a different designation in the cited contrast.

cautions: The Quranic plural رجال is represented under the singular citation headword رَجُل; one Quranic occurrence uses it in the construction meaning people proceeding on foot.
The pedestrian form in 17:64 is cited under the normalized dictionary form رَاجِل; the supplied QAC location, rather than Lane's historical citation notation, determines the Quran example location.

The classical entry contains many specialized, figurative, dialectal, and derived-form branches; these are kept separate from the Quranic senses unless the evidence explicitly supports their Quranic use.
